answer_text:
Let \(f\) be entire and satisfy

\[
|f(z)|\le |z|^a \qquad (z\in \mathbb C),
\]

where \(a>0\) is not an integer.

Since \(a>0\), letting \(z\to 0\) gives \(f(0)=0\). Write the Taylor expansion of \(f\) at \(0\):

\[
f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_n z^n.
\]

For any \(R>0\), Cauchy’s estimate gives

\[
|c_n|
\le \frac{1}{R^n}\max_{|z|=R}|f(z)|
\le \frac{R^a}{R^n}
= R^{a-n}.
\]

Thus for every integer \(n\ge 0\),

\[
|c_n|\le R^{a-n}\qquad \text{for all }R>0.
\]

Now use that \(a\) is not an integer.

- If \(n<a\), let \(R\to 0^+\). Then \(R^{a-n}\to 0\), so \(c_n=0\).
- If \(n>a\), let \(R\to \infty\). Then \(R^{a-n}\to 0\), so \(c_n=0\).

Since \(a\) is not an integer, every \(n\ge 0\) satisfies either \(n<a\) or \(n>a\). Hence every coefficient \(c_n\) is zero.

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{f\equiv 0}.
\]
